8 observations from Detroit Lions minicamp Tuesday

Observations from Birkett

■I don't know if Josh Wilson, Quandre Diggs or someone else will be the nickel back this year, but Wilson is making this team. He played with the No. 1 punt return team today and did a good job jamming gunners at the line of scrimmage.

■Dan Orlovsky took second-team reps at quarterback. The Lions won't decide their backup quarterback job until training camp, but Caldwell has a comfort level with Orlovsky that might be tough for Kellen Moore to beat.

■Tight end David Ausberry still has to be considered a longshot to make the team, but he made a nice open-field move to juke a defender today.

■Rashean Mathis isn't showing any signs of slowing down at (almost) 35 years old. Mathis made a nice recovery to bat down a deep Matthew Stafford pass (albeit one that was underthrown) to Calvin Johnson early in practice, and he broke up another comeback route to Ebron with good anticipation in seven-on-seven drills.

■Ameer Abdullah took the first rep at running back in full-team drills. Joique Bell is still the starter, but Abdullah has done nothing but impress this spring.

■Caraun Reid took every first-team rep at defensive tackle next to Haloti Ngata today. It's too early to declare him a starter, but he'll certainly be in the mix this fall.

■It was interesting watching Kyle Brindza kick into the extra-slim goalposts the Lions are using to work on their accuracy this year. The posts are about half the width of regulation goalposts (they measured almost nine steps by long snapper Don Muhlbach), and Brindza only practiced with them (when I was watching) from about 20-25 yards out. He didn't make every kick, but those slim goalposts make you appreciate how tough a job kickers have.
Oh.and maybe most importantly(for all you haters), Ebron didn't drop a single pass.

I really hope Abdullah gets used well this year. He seems like such an amazing talent, but I feel like the coaches will be very hesitant to use Bell less, even if Abdullah is outperforming him.

And that's definitely good to hear that Ebron didn't drop any passes. If he can make some good leaps forward, which it seems like he is just based on his improved hands, he could be a really good TE for us. We saw some glimpses of what he can do last year when he made moves like hurdling over defenders, so hopefully he can become more consistent.
